exposure: Severe insulin resistance (insulin requirements ≥2 units/kg) at delivery
outcome: Prevalence of severe insulin resistance at delivery
Glycemic control (HbA1c, fasting and postprandial glucose values)
Adverse perinatal outcomes (large for gestational age birth weight, cesarean delivery, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy)
cohort: Women with type-2 diabetes mellitus who delivered between January 2015 and December 2017 at a tertiary academic medical center
finding: Severe insulin resistance was common among pregnant women with type-2 diabetes (45%), and it was associated with suboptimal glycemic control but not with higher rates of adverse perinatal outcomes.
mod_finding: The rates of cesarean delivery did not differ between women with and without severe insulin resistance.
